newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Britain's Virgin Atlantic launches new look.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Virgin Atlantic launches new look.

text.p: British airline Virgin Atlantic launched its new livery in South Africa on Monday with a look inspired by the two-fingered "V for Victory" salute and the Virgin Vargas girl flying a Union Jack.
The move came a month after main rival British Airways Plc (BA) ditched its nationalistic red, white and blue colours.

"The logo highlights Virgin Atlantic's patriotic pride in British achievements...and the two-fingered salute is a powerful reminder of an underdog succeeding against the odds," the airline said in a statement.

British Airways said in June it was swapping its heraldic crest for ethnic art from around the world combined with Britain's national colours to project a more "creative and friendly" international image.

Virgin's facelift was its first since taking wing in 1984 with a flamboyant maiden London-New York flight which featured pop entertainment, spoon bending by psychic Uri Geller and food from the exclusive Maxim's restaurant.

The redesign was the latest salvo fired in Virgin's long-standing rivalry with BA which hit a public peak in 1993 when Virgin won a libel case over an alleged dirty tricks campaign by Britain's national carrier.
Virgin's new launch was not simply a knee-jerk reaction to British Airways' corporate revamp, according to David James, Virgin general manager for southern Africa.
"It's actually in response to customer feedback, and it's opportune now that BA has removed the flag from their planes," he said at the ceremony in Johannesburg.
James said Virgin's entire fleet of 20 aircraft would be repainted with the new design by the end of August.
He said the cost was insignificant. "It's a hell of a lot less than the 60 million pounds that BA is spending on its revised livery."
